**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 19, 2026**

- **Member:** Avery Grant
- **Member ID:** W620390523
- **Reference number:** POC-6B4F896296-38363
- **Denied service:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
- **Plan:** Moda Health (Commercial/ACA), Alaska
- **Governing policy:** CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion Guidelines (eviCore), V1.0.2025, effective 07/01/2025 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-601%20Ant%20Cerv%20Disc_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.26.2025.pdf

---

Dear Appeal Unit,

I am appealing the denial of the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 19, 2026 states that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking for reconsideration, because when I compare the plan's own published criteria in CMM-601 to what is already in my medical records, the records line up with those criteria. My surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed.

Below I have set out the plan's criteria in the plan's own words, followed by what my records show.

## 1. Daily pain with functional impairment

The policy states:

> "Significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)"

My records document 24 months of progressive neck pain that is not relieved by rest, along with radiating pain and numbness into my right thumb and index finger with weakness. The policy also lists, in the plan's words:

> "U nremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability"

The radiating pain, numbness and weakness in my right arm and hand are exactly the kind of upper-extremity symptoms this criterion describes. For the specific daily activities I can no longer do, please see [description of limited daily activities as documented in the office notes].

## 2. Objective physical exam findings

The policy states:

> "Objective physical exam findings include ANY of the following:"

One of the findings the policy lists is:

> "Nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling’s maneuver)"

My exam records document positive provocative testing on the affected side, together with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level seen on imaging. The name of the specific provocative test performed is recorded as [name of provocative maneuver documented in the exam note]. I would note that this criterion requires only one qualifying finding ("ANY of the following"), and the exam findings in my chart are objective, not merely reported symptoms.

## 3. Trial of conservative treatment

The policy states:

> "Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

Two of the items the plan lists under that heading are:

> "P rescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for six (6) weeks"

> "Provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks"

My records show both, and more than the six weeks the plan asks for:

- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief. I also had a corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026, which gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief. (The prescribing details for my NSAID therapy are at [NSAID name, dose and prescriber as documented in the medication list].)
- **Supervised exercise program:** physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training, 10 weeks, from April 30, 2026 to July 9, 2026, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

In other words, I completed at least two of the listed measures for longer than the stated six weeks, and my symptoms are described in the records as progressive rather than improved.

## 4. Imaging

The policy states:

> "MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual’s symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following:"

My MRI of the cervical spine dated June 5, 2026 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. That is nerve compression on the right side at the level being operated on, and it matches my symptoms: right-sided radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger with weakness, plus positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This is the concordance between imaging, symptoms and exam that the criterion asks for.

The policy also states:

> "P lain X-rays of the cervical spine including flexion/extension lateral views have been performed"

If the plan considers this item outstanding, the date and result of my cervical X-rays with flexion/extension lateral views is at [date and report of cervical X-rays including flexion/extension lateral views], and my provider's office can send that report on request.

## 5. Other listed requirements

The policy states:

> "A bsence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)"

My records document no untreated substance use. Any additional behavioral health documentation the plan wants is at [behavioral health history/clearance as documented in the chart].

The policy states:

> "Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following:"

and one of the two ways the plan allows this to be shown is:

> "Individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery as evidenced by blood cotinine lab results of ≤10 ng/mL"

My records document that I am a non-smoker. If a laboratory value is required, my cotinine result is at [date and result of blood cotinine lab, if obtained].

My records also note no active infection and a BMI of 29.

## A note on the criteria themselves

Several of the CMM-601 excerpts available to me end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not able to obtain in full. I am not going to guess at what those sub-items say, and I have not quoted any policy language other than what appears above. Because the denial notice does not identify which specific criterion or criteria my request failed, I am asking the plan to state plainly, in writing, which element of CMM-601 it found unmet and what documentation it considers missing. If the answer is a document rather than a clinical fact, my surgeon's office can supply it.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Moda Health overturn the denial dated August 19, 2026 (reference POC-6B4F896296-38363) and approve CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Lindqvist. In the alternative, I ask for a written explanation identifying the exact CMM-601 criterion relied on, and for review by a physician with training in spine surgery.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 15, 2027**. I am submitting this appeal to the Moda Health Appeal unit at P.O. Box 40384, Portland, OR 97240, or by fax to 503-412-4003 or 866-923-0412 (member line: 855-294-1668), using the grievance form that covers Moda plans in Oregon, Washington, and Alaska.

Please contact me if anything further would help, and please send your decision in writing. My surgeon's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone] and has authorized release of my records for this appeal.

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Avery Grant**
Member ID: W620390523
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [MRI report dated 2026-06-05; physical therapy discharge note; office/exam notes from Dr. Lindqvist; medication list; injection record dated 2026-05-14; other records as available]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
